big_idea: You'll never get fully on top of things or reach a future point of complete control, so the way to a meaningful life is imperfectionism: engaging fully with your limited, messy, present life now, through small daily shifts in attitude rather than waiting for ideal conditions.

tool.label: The done list
tool.text: Keep a running log of what you actually completed each day, instead of only tracking what's still undone.
tool.note: One of several short, practice-sized techniques across the book's 28 daily entries, meant to be revisited a little at a time rather than read straight through.

ideas.title: Imperfectionism
ideas.text: Treat your limitations of time, energy, and ability as the fixed terrain a meaningful life is built on, not problems to fix. The day when everything else is out of the way is never coming.

ideas.title: Effectiveness over efficiency
ideas.text: The goal isn't doing things faster, it's doing the right things. The book repeatedly pushes back on hustle-culture optimization for its own sake.

ideas.title: A kayak, not a superyacht
ideas.text: Life is inherently unsteady and reactive, more like paddling a small kayak on rough water than steering a stable ship. Trying to eliminate all instability is a losing game.

ideas.title: Scruffy hospitality
ideas.text: Borrowed from an Anglican priest: welcome and engage with life despite imperfect circumstances, rather than waiting until things are presentable or ready.

ideas.title: Treat inputs like a river, not a bucket
ideas.text: Books, opportunities, and obligations are an endless flowing stream to dip into selectively, not a fixed bucket you're guilty for failing to empty.

ideas.title: Decisions are made through action
ideas.text: Deliberation alone doesn't make something real. A choice only truly becomes a decision once you act on it, so momentum from small actions matters more than a perfect plan.

try_it: Start a daily done list for one week, alongside or instead of your to-do list.
Pick one task you're deliberating over and just do a small piece of it today, treating the action itself as the decision.
Find one area where you're waiting for ideal conditions and do a scruffier, imperfect version of it now.
Each morning this week, name one thing you'll consciously let go of, without guilt.
best_for: Readers who already read Four Thousand Weeks and want a lighter, repeatable companion
Busy list-makers who've slid back into old productivity anxiety
Anyone who wants bite-sized daily reflections rather than one long argument
less_useful: Readers new to Burkeman looking for his most substantial argument; start with Four Thousand Weeks first
Anyone wanting one big unifying framework rather than a collection of short daily entries

related.why: The deeper, mortality-centered argument this book applies day to day
Another short daily practice built around presence over control
